gloss: Stability a portal opens with. A raw integer, not fp — it is a countdown, and the only arithmetic performed on it is subtraction of the decay. fp(3000) as written, which at the decay below is 3000 engagement ticks, five fictional minutes.

Half-width of the uniform jitter applied to the opening stability on stream 10, so two raids from one snapshot do not end on the same tick. fp(600), giving 2400-3600 ticks. The termination bound is computed from initial PLUS jitter, so jitter can never make a raid outlast its declared ceiling.

Subtracted from portal stability every engagement tick, unconditionally. AN AUTHORED RAW INTEGER, never derived by fixed-point division: div rounds toward negative infinity, so a decay computed as stability/desired-length silently becomes 0 the moment the divisor exceeds the numerator, and a decay of 0 is a raid that runs forever with no error and no symptom. The loader rejects anything below 1.

Hard ceiling on combatants one side may field, summons included. Bounded per-tick work times a bounded tick count is what makes total raid work bounded. It is also the number the 64-slot observation block and the sim-core benchmark jointly have to live with.

Summons one side may hold at once. A summon over the cap is a no-op, never a queued request — a queue is an unbounded structure wearing a cap's clothes. MUST EQUAL primitive.json's `summon` cap, which clamps the stacked magnitude while this bounds the roster; the loader refuses a set where they disagree. They read 16 and 8 until 0.4.0. Both now say 8, the lower — no spec names a number, and too tight reads as weak summoning while too loose reads as a raid nobody can follow.
Objectives generated per raid. Six because the engagement observation block gives objectives 30 of its 64 slots at 5 fields each, and the block may not grow.
Side of the square battlefield in fp metres. fp(200), the reference extent contracts.md section 0 declares.

Side of one terrain cell in fp metres. fp(10) over a 200 m field is a 20x20 grid, coarse enough that line of sight is decided by a handful of cells and fine enough that cover is a place rather than a half of the map.
Probability per terrain cell of being impassable rock. fp probability at scale 1024; 82 is about 8%.
Probability per passable terrain cell of blocking line of sight — woodland, ruins. About 15%. Impassable cells always block as well.
Probability per passable terrain cell of being rough going. About 20%.

Multiplier on the movement allowance while crossing rough ground. fp(512) is half speed. Ordinary ground is fp(1024) and is not authored, because a multiplier of one is the identity rather than a tuning knob.
Depth of each side's deployment band, measured in from its own edge. fp(40) of a 200 m field leaves 120 m of contested ground between the two.

Metres a combatant may cover in one engagement tick on ordinary ground. fp(4) per 100 ms is 40 m/s, which is fast; it is a placeholder chosen so that a raid crosses the field in a legible number of ticks, not a claim about how people move.

The largest radius any effect may reach. The spatial index's cell size, so that a radius query inspects at most nine cells. Every other radius below must be at or under it, and the loader checks that.

Range of a targeted cast, in fp metres. fp(50). A single number rather than a per-node field because contracts.md section 2.3 declares no range on an effect, and inventing one here would be a sixteenth combat statistic outside the primitive registry — the exact move that makes winRateByPrimitive stop meaning anything.
Radius of an area-denial field, in fp metres. fp(12).
Range at which a knowledge-steal attempt may be made, in fp metres. fp(16) — closer than a cast, because reading a mind is an intimacy.
How close a combatant must stand to work on an objective, in fp metres. fp(8).
Progress one combatant in contact adds to an objective per engagement tick, against a completion of fp(1024). Four ticks alone, fewer in company.
Hit points a mage combatant starts from before species and depth. fp(64).
Hit points added per tier of the deepest node the mage knows. fp(8) per tier, so a tier-7 archmage carries roughly twice a novice's.

Concealment a combatant carries before any node grants it. Zero: concealment is a thing magic does, not a thing everyone has a little of. Authored rather than assumed so that the harness can raise it and see what a world with ambient cover looks like.
Hit points of a summoned combatant. fp(24).
Direct damage a summon deals per tick to a target in range. fp(2). A summon holds no knowledge, so this is the only thing it does.
Hit points of a soldier detachment. fp(48) — tougher than a summon and softer than a mage, and it stands for a hundred people rather than one.
Direct damage a soldier detachment deals per tick to a target in range. fp(3).

People one detachment is drawn from, and the number its cohort loses if it is destroyed. A cohort is never promoted to individuals (contracts.md section 1.3); it lends a counted portion of itself and gets the survivors back.
Reach of a soldier detachment, in fp metres. fp(8) — they have to close.
Objective value per knowledge instance a library holds. fp(1) each.
Objective value per tier summed across the instances a library holds, so a deep library is worth more than a broad one. fp(0.25) a tier.
Objective value of the defender's deepest living mage. fp(4).
Objective value of a university itself, apart from the library it holds. fp(2).

Fraction of the total value on the field the attacker must take, loot or burn to win. fp(512) is half. A fraction rather than an absolute, so that a poor universe is not unraidable and a rich one is not free.

Ceiling on the probability that a grimoire survives a burning attempt, whatever its durability. fp(922) is 90%, the same ceiling contracts.md section 3 puts on ward — a dwarven book resists fire; it is not fireproof.

Vigor a cast costs before tier. fp(2). contracts.md section 2.3 gives a node a researchCost, a teachCost and a scribeCost and no cast cost, so the price of releasing a spell is derived from its tier here rather than invented as a fourth node field — a field this change has no authority to add and no measurement to author.
Vigor added per tier of the node being cast. fp(1) a tier, so a tier-7 working costs five times a tier-1 one.

Engagement ticks a raider stays before she starts scoring withdrawal above everything else. Elapsed ticks, not remaining portal stability: measured, the portal opens with 2,411-3,577 ticks of life against raids of p50 64 and max 148, so the old fp(400) remaining-stability window opened thousands of ticks after every raid had ended - 0 of 169 raiders withdrew across 97 raids. Retuning could not fix it; portal jitter alone is +/-600 ticks. See scripts/w182-withdrawal.mjs.
How close to the portal's position a raider must stand to count as having withdrawn through it. fp(8) metres.

How many other universes hang in the sky beside this one. contracts.md section 1.1 puts one universe in a simulation instance, so the multiverse is never in state; this is how many rivals the composition root fabricates so action 14 has somewhere to point and something can raid back. Three, because a target list of one makes the god's choice of target vacuous. INVENTED: pvp-server owns real pairing against persisted peer snapshots, and this stands in for it in headless Monte Carlo only.

Mages a rival universe re-roles to raider, and therefore the size of the warband it can field through a portal. Under max-combatants-per-side by design: a rival that saturated the cap would make every raid a question about the cap. INVENTED alongside rival-universe-count and untuned for the same reason.

Combat-carrying nodes granted to each rival raider, at full mastery, drawn in content order from the nodes whose effects carry direct-damage, ward, concealment or knowledge-steal. Granted rather than researched because a rival built at world tick zero has researched nothing, and a warband that arrives holding no castable node is a walkover that would read as a balance result. Full mastery because CASTABLE_MASTERY is the activation threshold and an instance below it deploys inert.

Probability per world tick that a rival opens a portal into this universe, drawn on stream 10 (objective and raid generation). fp(0.0039) — about one inbound raid every 256 world ticks, so roughly nine over the 2400-tick reference horizon. This is the arrival process vision section 8 leaves unspecified and demands be BOUNDED: it is the griefing surface, and inboundRaidTempoLoss exists to measure it. Untuned, and the first number a balance sweep should move.

World ticks after any raid during which no further inbound raid may open. Five world years. Vision section 8 requires inbound raid frequency to be bounded rather than merely improbable — a Bernoulli process alone admits a run of arrivals that strips a universe with no floor under it, which is the live-PvP death sentence that section names. A cooldown is a hard bound the arrival rate cannot defeat.

Grimoires a warband carries home per library it reaches. Vision section 8 gives the attacker two verbs -- destroying OR looting -- and this is where they divide: the first four books off the shelf are taken, the rest face a fire their durability may survive. Four because it is a fraction of a mature library rather than all of it, so both verbs stay reachable in one raid. This is the number that decides how fast knowledge crosses between universes.

Books a rival shelves from cells this universe's own ruleset forbids. Not zero, because twelve of seventy cells are enabled and they hold 51 of 300 nodes, so an undisturbed universe learns all 51 and stops: the plateau is content exhaustion, not balance. A god researches only what they permit but may take what another permitted, so this is what makes the other 249 reachable at all. INVENTED with the rest of the rival stand-in.

Engagement tick at which the muster phase ends whether or not the two sides have met. The natural boundary is contact itself, and this is the guard on its degenerate case: sides that never close, or a raid whose objectives are all undefended, would otherwise sit in muster with the full verb set for the whole raid. At the shipped movement rate the bands close in about twenty ticks, so this rarely binds and is not meant to.

Engagement tick at or after which the raid is in its resolution phase and the player has no verbs left. Elapsed ticks for the same reason withdraw-after-ticks is, and it carried the same falsehood: fp(600) of remaining stability glossed as the last six hundred ticks of a two-to-three-thousand tick raid, against raids of p50 64. Resolution was a phase no raid entered. Kept a separate constant so a change to either does not silently retune the other.

Favor the defender pays to forbid a technique, a form, or a cell mid-raid. Priced at the world-scale interdiction rate rather than derived from it, because it is a different verb: it resolves in seconds, it is irreversible for the engagement, and it is the input to the post-raid revert surcharge. Charged only when the lock accepts the change; a refused change costs a decision and not a resource.

Favor the defender pays to permit mid-raid. Identical to forbidding, because vision pillar 1 rests on the permit/forbid decision being symmetric, and any price difference turns denial from a peer strategy into a penalty.

Favor the defender pays to levy one detachment out of a cohort that does not fight -- laborers, scholars, whoever the universe was using for something else. Muster only: deciding who fights is a thing you do before contact or not at all. NOT a second soldier detachment: the opening deployment already commits every detachment a soldier cohort can field, so that verb could never fire. Priced below a ruleset change because it commits people rather than law.
Favor the defender pays to raise every living defender's ward by one stacked source. Survives into contact: it helps the people already fighting, which is what the contact phase is for.

Ward the defender's ward verb adds, as one more stacked source rather than a written total, so it caps through primitives like every other ward. fp(0.2) -- a fifth of incoming damage turned aside, once, at a price the defender will feel.

Vis the attacker spends to mend every living raider. The verb that makes the attacker's two payments pull against each other: Vis keeps raiders alive to cast again, and every cast is a spell the host's academics watch you use. It was a vigor refill first; measured over eight seeds, a raider never spends enough vigor in a 54-96 tick raid for a refill to do anything, so the verb reported no-effect on every run. Hit points are what binds.

Hit points restored per raider by the mend verb, capped at the health she arrived with. fp(32) against a combatant-base-max-hp of fp(64) is half a raider's frame -- large enough that the buy is visible in survival, which is the observable section 5's first claim is stated in, and small enough that it is a reprieve rather than immortality.
Vis the attacker spends to raise every raider's concealment. Muster only: how you approach is decided before you are seen.

Concealment the conceal verb adds per raider, clamped at concealment-cap. fp(0.15) -- a real evasion chance against the only miss roll in combat, and small enough that it is a lean rather than a build.

Ceiling on a combatant's concealment however it was raised. fp(0.8): above this a raider is effectively untargetable and area denial becomes the only counter, which would make one verb the whole game. Section 3 caps concealment for primitives through the stacking table; this is the same ceiling applied to the row field the conceal verb writes.

Vis a raiding party carries through the portal. A portable, lootable stock, seeded once and never refilled -- running out is what ends an over-extended raid. AUTHORED CONTENT RATHER THAN A WORLD BALANCE, and deliberately so: the economy spec amendment records that Vis production and storage land with the economy capability, and reading a stock that does not exist yet would be a fourth resource invented here rather than one chosen. fp(64) buys sixteen of the cheaper verb.
